A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUSVIBES benchmark and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganization and redrawing.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of coding agents, security-prompting experiments, vulnerability analyses, and benchmark statistics.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of Gemini 3 Pro under three agent frameworks.

M1.justification: The vulnerability-mining, feature-masking, task-generation, adaptive-verification, and execution-validation procedures remain the same. Reorganized explanations and renamed prompt headings do not establish a changed method; the full prompts retain the same operative instructions.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 200 Python feature-request tasks covering 77 CWEs and 10 domains. V2 corrects Appendix A.3's project count from 105 to 108, matching v1's main text; this does not establish added repositories or tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds Gemini 3 Pro as an evaluated backbone under SWE-Agent, OpenHands, and Claude Code in Table 5. The original Claude 4 Sonnet, Kimi K2, and Gemini 2.5 Pro comparisons remain intact.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated backbone for the shared-correct-task framework comparison from Gemini 2.5 Pro to Claude 4 Sonnet, retaining the 8.9/19.4/10.4 scores. This is a reported setting correction, without evidence of rerunning. Gemini 3 configurations are added; the stated pass@1 metrics and 200-step default remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The generic-to-oracle transition analysis receives revised evidence. The existing Wagtail case also gains its matching patch and test outcomes in v2 Figure 11, replacing v1 Figure 10's duplicated aiohttp-session illustration. The remaining case studies and mitigation questions are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without agent-evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. V2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 Table 5 adds Gemini 3 Pro FuncPass/SecPass results of 38.0/11.0, 53.5/9.0, and 34.5/4.5 for SWE-Agent, OpenHands, and Claude Code. Original Table 3 scores remain unchanged. Transition percentages change, including secure-to-incorrect from 3.4% to 3.0% (v1 Table 6 versus v2 Figure 8). The new text incorrectly describes functional increases as 195% and 230%; Table 5 implies approximately 95% and 130%.

T1.justification: The commit, patch, mask, and test relationships and the shared-functionally-correct-subset metric definition remain unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, functionality-security gap, and inadequacy of simple prompting mitigations. The introduction corrects six combinations to nine, already represented in v1 Table 3.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the Gemini comparison as showing limits of reasoning post-training for security. Section 5 replaces the oracle-more-severe explanation with greater security improvement due to imperfect self-selection. The introduction qualifies its causal explanation as a hypothesis, and a new Impact Statement recommends mandatory security review. Appendix limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies Claude Sonnet 4 for task creation and verification, and the title page adds a leaderboard link. Conversely, Appendix A.3 replaces the explicit OpenAI o3 parser-model identification with a generic LM citation, reducing that detail's precision.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Gemini 3 Pro reference. Existing benchmark positioning remains unchanged; publication-metadata updates and consolidation of duplicate SWE-Agent references do not represent different cited works.

P1.justification: Selected introductory, construction, and analysis passages are rewritten. Verification becomes a separate Section 3.2, CWE statistics move ahead of the appendix prompts and cases, and an Impact Statement is added. The overall narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Visual presentation is extensively revised: pipeline and verification diagrams are redrawn, Venn diagrams and prompt/code panels are restyled, the transition table becomes a labeled heatmap, and a Gemini comparison table is added. Case figures are reformatted and relocated, including replacement of the mismatched Wagtail illustration.

improvement.justification: V2 fixes the mismatched Wagtail illustration and aligns the transition matrix with the aggregate mitigation scores, while adding Gemini 3 evidence and clearer curation documentation. These improve evidential completeness and consistency. However, the new discussion overstates functional percentage increases as 195%/230% instead of approximately 95%/130%, tempering the overall gain.
